title: Two timing tests only fail when the whole suite runs
goal: Running all the tests at once sometimes reports two failures that are not real: the same two tests pass every time they are run on their own. Anyone building the app has to learn which failures to ignore, which is exactly how a real failure gets ignored too. Make these two tests judge what they are actually measuring so a red run means something is broken.
notes:
Reproduced on 2026-09-15 on main at 6b3deb32 plus the copy-a-look work.

Full run:
  $ Scripts/test.sh
  ✘ Test "A whole strip of moving previews fits inside one frame of the loop" recorded an issue at IconPreviewRenderTests.swift:258:27: Issue recorded
  ✘ Test aGridOverALargeScreenshotPaysForTheBorderQuery() recorded an issue at DrawLandingCostTests.swift:151:9: Expectation failed: (abs(dense - sparse) → 2662.0996093750005) < (dense * 0.5 → 1463.3499375)
  ✘ Test run with 7028 tests in 564 suites failed after 84.362 seconds with 2 issues.

Same binary, same commit, the two suites on their own:
  $ Scripts/test.sh --filter DrawLandingCostTests --filter IconPreviewRenderTests
  ✔ Test run with 10 tests in 3 suites passed after 8.120 seconds.

An earlier full run of nearly the same tree passed all 7027, so it is load dependent rather than a real regression. Both are wall-clock or work-count budgets measured while 564 suites share the machine. The renderer perf suite already solves this: it calibrates against a yardstick and reports the machine multiplier (see the [perf] lines it prints). These two do not.
acceptance: Scripts/test.sh run twice in a row while the machine is busy reports the same result both times
The two tests still catch the thing they were written to catch, shown by making the cost they guard genuinely worse and watching them fail
No test in the suite fails on a machine that is merely loaded

log.note: Hit again on 2026-09-15 during 'several shapes turn into one path': Scripts/test.sh full run failed only aGridOverALargeScreenshotPaysForTheBorderQuery (DrawLandingCostTests.swift:151, abs(dense-sparse) 2508.4 < dense*0.5 1935.7), and the same filter alone passed 3/3 in 8.2s. Same shape as the two already recorded here.

Seen again on 2026-09-15: aGridOverALargeScreenshotPaysForTheBorderQuery failed in the full run (dense 5068us vs sparse 4814us worst round, gap 2942us against a 1387us allowance) and passed on its own seconds later (dense 2608us, sparse 2388us). The same run took 72s for that test inside the suite and 8s alone, so what it is really measuring is how loaded the machine is, not how much the border query costs.
